basis: Select the record-defined Lillias Stewart as the probable mother of James Glasgow-1483 at 86% subjective confidence. The 1790 Govan baptism explicitly names Samuel Glasgow and Lilias Stewart; the independently recorded Barony banns name that same distinctive full parent pair shortly before either disputed baptism date. This supports one local household across the two registers. James’s adult account has a Govan nailer burial in 1833, aged 42, and children Samuel and Lillias with Jean Cunningham. Parish, approximate age and the paired family names favour identification with the 1790 child. The granddaughter’s Lillias name is supporting naming evidence, not proof.
limitations: The 86% assesses the complete maternity proposition for the adult James, including the child-to-adult identity. It is not the near-certain named maternal role for the indexed 1790 child alone. The baptism dates 22 March and 25 April remain unresolved versions of one underlying event; no original was inspected. The banns identify neither man as a nailer. James’s burial age suggests about 1790–1791 and is not an exact match to the indexed child. A different James or Samuel remains possible. No birth, death, parents or childhood identity is assigned to Lillias from the contributed 1766 estimate.
next_test: Inspect the original Govan baptism for its date, residence and paternal occupation, then the 1814 James–Jean Cunningham marriage and children’s entries for an occupation, witness or lair link. Test the older Samuel’s identity separately. A 1797 Barony Samuel banns entry (OPR 622/7, item 1, p 88) remains unassigned: do not infer a remarriage, Lillias’s death or a second household for this nailer from the shared name alone.
